newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed lower on Monday, dragged down in the last hour of business by a Wall Street-inspired decline in other European bourses.

Dealers said nervousness ahead of a Federal Reserve meeting about U.S. interest rates tomorrow had unsettled investors around Europe. Concern about the health of Russian president Boris Yeltsin also cast a dampener on the session.

The AEX share index closed 4.03 points, or 0.71 percent, lower at 561.67. "It's been a pretty quiet session and people have had a lot of time to dwell on things like the chances of a U.S. rate hike and Yeltsin's heart operation," said a dealer.

Dealers said uncertainty over Russia could be prolonged with doctors saying Yeltsin's operation could be delayed for weeks. "The main thing at this moment is Yeltsin's health, that's concerning quite a lot of people at this moment. It could be two months before the doctors do the operation," said one.
"There's a lot of uncertainty coming from that and it's keeping the buyers out of the market," he added.

Volumes were low from the outset with many in the market content early on to let prices drift, powered only by a weakening bond market. Dealers said lethargy after last Friday's options expirations also kept trading quiet.
"People are talking about a possible rise in (U.S.) interest rates and they're beginning to talk in terms of a 1/2 point rather than a 1/4 point," said a dealer.

Technical analysts mainly turned out neutral forecasts for the week, with some rowing back from more bullish stances last week. ING Barings said the inability of the AEX to break the 572 record last week showed overhead resistance was intact for the moment. It changed its view to sideways from up last week.
Others agreed. "The main resistance is at 571/572 and it doesn't look like it's going to be broken. If it's not we can go back to 558 and then there's a long way down," said a dealer.
Blue chip gainers were thin on the ground but Philips put on 40 cents to close at 59.70 guilders. Dealers said recent presentations to analysts had been favourably received.

Cyclical shares moved up at the outset, encouraged by the prospects of further Dutch economic growth laid out in last week's budget. They came back late in the session on profit-taking with DSM down 3.00 guilders 165.00, down from an early session high of 169.20, although packager KNP BT held onto 40 cents of its initial 60 cent gain to close at 40.60 guilders.
Financials felt the pinch from lower bonds and interest rate jitters with ABN AMRO down 1.10 guilders to 91.70. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
